messages:
Maria L.: Heads-up: running a replay+JSON tool-calling sweep and seeing unexplained p99 jumps when KV-hit ratio changes. Need a strict apples-to-apples bench plan before we tweak kernels.

Kevin T.: Proposed two-pass methodology: (A) cold run (KV disabled), (B) warm run (populate cache then replay same trace). Use identical model binary, tokenizer, flags, and seed for both.

Alex R.: Important: log kernel selection per request. We saw auto-switching where for seq_len<80 flash_attention init cost made matmul_triton faster. If batching leads to many small batches runtime sometimes picks the suboptimal kernel.

Sophie M.: JSON-mode note: our strict validator is synchronous and lives on the CPU path, it can add ~8-15ms per request and block batching windows. That inflates tail latencies and can trigger retries when minor schema flaps happen.

Maria L.: Can you paste the exact harness command and env vars you used so I can reproduce? Also pin seeds.

Kevin T.: Example run I used (cold):
```
export REPLAY_SEED=2026
export KV_CACHE_POLICY=disabled
export FORCE_KERNEL=""
./harness/replay --trace traces/2026/chat-sample.jsonl \
  --rps 200 --duration 300 --preserve-order \
  --model /mnt/models/opt-13b.pt --tokenizer bpe \
  --emit=perf.prof --out out/replay-cold.jsonl
```
For warm set KV_CACHE_POLICY=warm and pre-fill via --preload-kv. To measure pure model path add --json-validation=off.

Alex R.: Forcing kernel for controlled tests:
```
export RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_attention
# or
export RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_triton
```
But for apples-to-apples leave unset and record chosen kernel per-request.

Kevin T.: Patch note for traces: add kv_hit and kernel_name to emitted events so we can later group latencies by kv/miss and kernel. E.g. emit: {"req_id": id, "kv_hit": true, "kernel": "flash_attention"} in the flatline JSON.

Sophie M.: Quick A/B I ran (10k reqs each, same seed):
- dynamic batch (delay=5ms): p50 36ms / p95 130ms / p99 340ms
- fixed-window (max_batch=48, interval=12ms): p50 42ms / p95 102ms / p99 160ms
- JSON strict validator on: p95 increases ~1.6x and retry-rate ~1.8% (mostly due to tiny schema glitches)
Fixed-window reduced tails by eliminating many tiny 1-2 request batches. Avg latency slightly higher but tails better.

perf-bot: Automated run complete id=run-2026-03-22-09, requests=10000, rps=200, KV=warm, json_validation=on, p50=40ms, p95=190ms, p99=380ms, errors=190 (1.9%), retried=172

Maria L.: Concern: retries re-run the entire token generation currently. If validator fails mid-postprocess the client retries end-to-end and we re-consume GPU. We should avoid full model retries. Options: cheap pre-validate, or streaming validator that checks chunks so failures don't force a re-gen.

Sophie M.: Two pragmatic mitigations: (1) implement a streaming JSON validator that runs on the CPU consumer thread and can fail fast without blocking batching; (2) add runtime hook to allow post-processing-only retries (if proto includes full token log) so we don't re-run model unless necessary. Both need infra changes.

Alex R.: Also ensure replay emits tokens_generated, tokens_cached, and validation_ms per request. That way we can compute wasted GPU tokens due to retries.

Kevin T.: Apples-to-apples checklist for runs: same model hash, same tokenizer & seed, identical trace file, same node maintenance state (no GC/snapshots), run both cold/warm, record kernel_name, batch_size, kv_hit, validation_time_ms, tokens_generated.

Maria L.: I'll open a short epic: 1) don't re-run full model on validation failure, 2) add streaming validator, 3) record kernel+kv flags in replay traces. Tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml.

Sophie M.: I'll run a controlled sweep tomorrow: RPS sweep 50/100/200, batching strategies dynamic vs fixed-window, json-validation on/off. Will attach perf.prof and out JSONL.

Maria L.: Thanks. When you post results include raw perf.prof + replay output and note whether any kernel forcing was used or whether kernels auto-switched. We'll use that to decide whether to adjust default batching heuristics or to nudge kernel-choice logic.
